name: LLMorpheus
one_liner: Mutation testing framework where an LLM proposes fault-injecting code mutants by filling placeholders in JavaScript source; mutants are run against the project test suite.

loop.proposes: An LLM is prompted at placeholders in chosen code locations and suggests replacement code, producing mutants of JavaScript packages.
loop.judged_by: The project test suite is run against each mutant to determine whether it is killed or survives.
loop.steers: Surviving mutants expose concrete gaps in the existing test suite.

headline_result: On 13 real-world JavaScript packages, produced mutants resembling real bugs that StrykerJS, a state-of-the-art mutation testing tool, cannot produce.
caveat: Distinguishing a genuinely surviving bug-revealing mutant from a semantically equivalent refactoring still requires diff inspection.
beyond_harness_note: An automated mutation-testing harness compiles and runs the test suite over every proposed AST mutant to classify killed vs. surviving faults.
algorithmic_authority: Compiler and automated mutation-testing execution engine

sources.title: LLMorpheus: Mutation Testing using Large Language Models (arXiv:2404.09952)

verification.notes: Re-checked against Tip, Bell and Schaefer, arXiv:2404.09952 (abstract). Corrections: card previously cited unrelated arXiv:2404.08846; title is "LLMorpheus: Mutation Testing using Large Language Models"; language is JavaScript only (not TypeScript); the abstract describes placeholder-filling by an LLM, not AST-location mutation, and does not mention ranking by survivability or compilation; the headline now states the StrykerJS comparison the abstract gives. The unconfirmed "IEEE TSE 2024" venue was removed (the arXiv page prints no venue). Year stays 2024 (first posted 2024-04-15).
